meetings.title: Q4 Roadmap Planning – Product & Engineering
segments: Morning everyone. Thanks for making time. The goal today is to lock the Q4 roadmap so engineering can start sprint planning on Monday.
We have three big bets on the table: the new reporting dashboard, the Slack integration, and the self-serve onboarding flow. We realistically can't ship all three.
Agreed. From the engineering side we have about 14 engineer-weeks of capacity once you subtract on-call and the tech debt we promised to pay down.
Before we pick, I pulled the numbers. 38 percent of churned accounts last quarter never finished onboarding. That's the biggest single signal we have.
That matches what we saw in usability testing. People get stuck at the data source connection step. Four out of six testers needed help there.
So onboarding looks like the clear winner on impact. What does it cost us, Priya?
If we keep the scope to the connection wizard and the sample workspace, I'd estimate six engineer-weeks. The risk is the OAuth work for the two new connectors.
Do we need both connectors in the first release, or can we ship with just the Postgres one?
Postgres alone covers about 70 percent of new signups, so yes, we could split it. That brings it down to roughly four and a half weeks.
I love that. I'd rather ship a smooth flow for most people than a half-finished one for everyone.
Okay, next item is the reporting dashboard. Marcus, what's the customer pressure looking like?
It's mostly enterprise. Three of our top ten accounts have asked for scheduled PDF reports, and one renewal in November is explicitly tied to it.
The scheduled export part is cheap. The custom chart builder is what makes it expensive. That's easily eight weeks on its own.
Then let's do scheduled exports this quarter and push the chart builder to Q1. Does anyone feel strongly otherwise?
No, but I'd like two days to sketch the chart builder now so we aren't designing it from scratch in January.
Totally fair. Priya, can you check whether the export service can reuse the existing PDF renderer?
I'll check with Arjun today. I think it can, but the renderer has a memory issue with large tables that we'd need to fix first.
Last one, the Slack integration. Honestly, I think this is the one we cut.
I'm a bit worried about that. Sales mentions Slack in almost every competitive deal. Is there a smaller version?
We could ship a simple webhook that posts a summary to a channel. That's maybe one week, no app directory listing, no slash commands.
That's a good compromise. Let's put the webhook in as a stretch goal if onboarding comes in on time.
One concern on timelines. Design is also supporting the marketing site refresh in October, so I'm stretched thin.
Understood. I'll talk to Nina about moving the site refresh to November so you can focus on onboarding first.
Great discussion. To recap: onboarding with Postgres first, scheduled exports, and the Slack webhook as a stretch. I'll send the written roadmap by Friday.
Sounds good. I'll have sprint tickets ready for Monday's planning.

meetings.title: Sales Demo – Acme Corp <> Northwind
segments: Hi Dana, hi Kevin, thanks for joining. I've also brought Alex, our head of product, to answer the deeper questions. How's your week going?
Busy, but good. We're in the middle of our annual planning, which is partly why we're looking at tools like yours right now.
Perfect timing then. Could you remind us what prompted the search? I want to make sure the demo focuses on what matters to you.
Our operations team spends about 12 hours a week building reports by hand in spreadsheets. It's slow, and the numbers are often wrong by the time leadership sees them.
And from the IT side, we need anything new to support single sign-on and keep data in our own region. That's non-negotiable for us.
Both of those are covered. We support SAML SSO with Okta and Azure AD, and enterprise workspaces can pin data to the EU or US region.
Let me share my screen. This is the main dashboard. Everything here refreshes automatically from your connected sources, so nobody has to rebuild the spreadsheet.
This is impressive. Can my team set up those scheduled reports themselves, or does it need an admin?
Any editor can schedule them. Admins just control which channels and email domains reports can go to.
What about the integration with our data warehouse? We're on Snowflake. Is that a native connector?
Snowflake is native, yes. It uses key-pair authentication and read-only roles, so you keep full control over what we can see.
Okay, let's talk numbers. What would this cost for around 40 users?
For 40 users on the Business plan it's $45 per seat per month, billed annually, so roughly $21,600 a year. SSO and regional hosting are included at that tier.
Honestly, that's more than we budgeted. We were expecting something closer to $15,000.
I understand. If you commit to a two-year term, I can bring it to $38 per seat, and we can include onboarding at no charge.
My concern is the security review. Last time a vendor review took us three months and delayed the whole project.
We can send our SOC 2 Type II report and a completed security questionnaire up front. That usually cuts the review down to a few weeks.
That would help a lot. Could you also send a case study from a company our size? Leadership will ask for one.
Absolutely. I'll send the Brightline Health case study, they're about 600 people and had a very similar reporting problem.
Great. If the security review goes smoothly, we'd want to start a pilot by the 15th of next month.
Perfect. I'll send a proposal with both pricing options and the security pack by Thursday, and let's book a follow-up for next week.

meetings.title: Engineering Standup – Sprint 42
segments: Morning all, let's keep it quick. Arjun, do you want to start?
Sure. Yesterday I finished the retry logic for the sync workers. Today I'm moving on to the PDF renderer memory issue. No blockers.
Nice. How bad is the memory issue?
Tables over about 5,000 rows push the renderer past 2 gigabytes. I think we're loading the whole dataset instead of streaming it. Should be a two-day fix.
I'm still on the onboarding wizard. The connection step UI is done, but I'm blocked on the OAuth callback because the staging redirect URL isn't whitelisted.
Who owns the staging OAuth config?
That's me. Sorry, I missed the ticket. I'll add the redirect URL right after standup, it's a five minute change.
Great, thanks Tom. Once that's in I should finish the wizard by Thursday.
From my side, the CI pipeline is down to 9 minutes from 14 after caching the dependency layer. Today I'm looking at the flaky end to end test on the billing page.
Quick product question. Sofia, does the wizard include the sample workspace option, or is that a separate ticket?
Separate ticket. I can pick it up next, but it probably won't land before Friday's demo.
That's fine, let's demo the connection flow alone on Friday and show the sample workspace next week.
One more thing, the production error rate went up to 1.2 percent last night after the deploy. Arjun, can you take a quick look?
Yes, I saw that. It looks like timeouts from the new connector health check. I'll raise the timeout and add an alert.
Thanks. That's it, have a great day everyone.

meetings.title: Interview – Senior Frontend Engineer (Maya Chen)
segments: Hi Maya, thanks for joining us. I'm Alex, I lead product, and Priya here leads engineering. We'll spend most of the time on your experience and a short design discussion.
Thanks for having me. I'm excited, I've actually used Northwind at my last company.
Oh nice! Could you walk us through your current role and the project you're most proud of?
I'm a senior engineer at a fintech startup. The project I'm proudest of is rebuilding our transaction table. We went from rendering 500 rows with lag to 100,000 rows smoothly using virtualization.
How did you measure that it was actually better for users?
We tracked interaction latency in production. The 95th percentile went from about 400 milliseconds to under 50. Support tickets about the page being slow dropped to almost zero.
Let's do a design question. How would you build a transcript viewer where clicking a line seeks a video, and the active line highlights while it plays?

I'd keep the current time in one piece of state owned by the page. The player updates it on time updates, and each transcript line just checks whether it's active. Clicking a line calls a seek function that the player exposes.
What happens with a two hour meeting and thousands of lines?
Then I'd virtualize the list and find the active line with a binary search on start times, so we're not checking every line on each tick. I'd also throttle auto-scroll so users can scroll freely.
Good answer. How do you handle disagreement with a product manager on scope?
I try to bring data. Once a PM wanted a feature in two weeks that I thought needed five. I split it into a smaller first version we could ship in two, and that's what we did.
What would my first 90 days look like?
You'd join the onboarding squad. First month is shipping small fixes, then owning the sample workspace feature end to end.
We're nearly out of time. Any concerns on your side about the role?
Only the timeline. I have another offer that expires next Friday, so I'd love to hear back before then.
Understood, that's helpful to know. We'll get back to you by Wednesday.

meetings.title: Customer Onboarding – Brightline Health
segments: Hi Omar, welcome to Northwind! Today we'll get your first data source connected and set up your first dashboard.
Thanks Rachel. We're excited. The board has been asking for a weekly patient-volume report and right now it takes my analyst two days.
Let's fix that. Which source holds the patient volume data?
It's in our Postgres reporting replica. Our IT team already created a read-only user for you.
Perfect. Go to Sources, choose Postgres, and paste the host and the read-only credentials. I'll stay on the line.
Hmm, it says connection refused. Is that on our side?
That's usually the firewall. You'll need to allow our two static IP addresses. I'll paste them in the chat now.
Okay, I've asked IT to whitelist them. They say it'll take about ten minutes.
It's connected now. Great, I can see all the tables.
Awesome. Let's build the patient-volume chart. Pick the visits table, group by week, and count distinct patient IDs.
That's exactly the number the board wants. This would have taken us two days. Can I schedule it every Monday morning?
Yes, click Schedule, choose weekly on Monday at 8 AM, and add the board distribution list.
One concern: some of this data is sensitive. Can I make sure only aggregated numbers go out by email?
Yes. Scheduled emails only include the chart image and totals. Row-level data never leaves the workspace, and we can also turn on PII masking for your account.
Please do turn on masking. Our compliance team will ask about it.
We'll check in again in two weeks to see how the first reports landed. Any final questions?
No, this was really helpful. Thank you both.

meetings.title: Spring Launch Campaign Retro
segments: Okay, let's do the retro for the spring launch. I'll start with the numbers, then we go through what worked and what didn't.
We got 4,200 signups in the first two weeks, which is 30 percent above target. Trial-to-paid conversion was 11 percent, slightly below our 13 percent goal.
Sales felt the bump too. We booked 18 demos from launch traffic, which is about double a normal month.
The launch video did really well. Average watch time was over 70 percent, which is great for a two minute video.
The pricing page. Several prospects told me they were confused about what was included in each plan.
Agreed. We changed the plan names a week before launch and the comparison table didn't fully update. That was a mistake on our side.
Also the onboarding emails went out late. The first email was delayed by two days because of a template bug.
That probably hurt conversion. Can we make sure that's tested before the next launch?
A launch checklist with a final review of the pricing page 48 hours before go-live.
And a short FAQ about plan differences that sales can send to prospects.
I'd like us to A/B test the pricing page layout over the next month. We have enough traffic now.
Great. I'll compile everything into a retro doc and share it by Monday.
